clue.text: Travel by stream, getting to a wild animal

parts.note: to go is to travel
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: Someone travels along a stream and comes upon a wild beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The great ape of African forests is an example of a wild animal.

clue.text: Time needed by Richard to create cunning plan

parts.note: Rick is a short form of the name Richard

explanation.surface: A man called Richard needs time to hatch a crafty scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse or ploy to deceive someone is a synonym for a cunning plan.

clue.text: Lobby in hospital department next to railway

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A waiting area sits inside a hospital department beside the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobby is an entrance hall, the way into a building, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Grandma eager to provide material

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother
keen means eager

explanation.surface: Granny is happy to supply some fabric for a sewing project.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth, originally from Nanjing, so a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Gate displays placard with name at end

indicators.note: says the letter for name comes after the placard word

parts.note: a poster is a placard

explanation.surface: A gate has a sign stuck on it with a name written at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a small back or side gate, especially in a castle wall.

clue.text: Soldier frayed at the edges is a veteran

indicators.note: a thing frayed at its edges has lost its outer threads, so the word soldier loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An old soldier, a bit worn round the edges, is a war veteran.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an informal term for an old person or thing, a veteran.

clue.text: Respond concerning piece of legislation

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a business letter
an act is a law passed by parliament

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to reply about a new law.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond to something is to react to it; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Husband initially felt irritation, being attached

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of the word husband

parts.note: itched means felt an irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: A husband was annoyed at first about being married.
explanation.walkthrough: Hitched also means married informally, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitched means fastened or tied on, so it fits being attached; it is also slang for married.

clue.text: Hopin' for a painkiller

definitions.meaning: hoping, with its final G dropped as the apostrophe shows, means aspiring said in the same casual way, without its last letter
a common analgesic tablet, acetylsalicylic acid

explanation.surface: Someone is wishing for something to take the pain away.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in Hopin' shows a dropped G; aspiring with its G dropped likewise gives the word for the tablet.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a familiar over-the-counter medicine taken to relieve pain.

clue.text: Protests rude mostly, but not entirely

indicators.note: only part of the phrase rude mostly is used, the letters sitting inside it

explanation.surface: Street protests are mostly rude, though not all of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Demos is the informal short form of demonstrations, public protests.

clue.text: Nasty dogs bite finally? Swear

parts.note: curs are mean, mongrel dogs

indicators.note: takes only the closing letter of the word bite

explanation.surface: Someone bitten by vicious dogs might well let rip with bad language.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse is to swear, use bad language; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Religious building has study with airhole

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn
a vent is an opening that lets air through

explanation.surface: A church building contains a study room with an air vent.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent is a building where nuns live a religious life.

clue.text: Monster making some progress

indicators.note: only some of the letters of progress are used, found inside it

explanation.surface: A monster is gradually advancing on its victims.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of fairy tales, a kind of monster.

clue.text: Conspirator, a beast mostly and American

indicators.note: most of the word for beast is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a brute is a beast
US stands for American, as in US citizen

explanation.surface: A plotter is described as largely a brute, and American too.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus was one of the conspirators who assassinated Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Work to include a bit of drama

indicators.note: the work word takes the letter a inside it

parts.note: to ply is to work at, as in ply a trade

explanation.surface: A piece of work needs a dramatic moment added.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a single piece of drama written for the stage.

clue.text: Aching between head and shoulders is a nuisance

parts.note: pain is an ache
the neck lies between the head and shoulders, so this phrase gives in the neck

explanation.surface: A sore neck is a real bother.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom describes an annoying person or thing, a nuisance.

clue.text: Stall on display is to be prominent

parts.note: a stand is a market stall
out means on show, as flowers are out

explanation.surface: A market stall on show is meant to be eye-catching.
explanation.definitionFit: To be conspicuous or noticeable is a synonym for being prominent.

clue.text: Offer to include information that could feature in car manual

definitions.text: that could feature in car manual

indicators.note: the offer word holds the information word inside it

parts.note: a bid is an offer, as at an auction
gen is informal British slang for information

explanation.surface: A proposal comes with details that might be printed in a car handbook.
explanation.definitionFit: The big end is the larger end of an engine's connecting rod, a part discussed in a motoring handbook.

clue.text: He's a kind to riot

indicators.note: to riot is to run wild, so the letters of he's a kind are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A man is described as the type who causes trouble in the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and a description: a skinhead was stereotyped as a youth prone to violence.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinhead, a shaven-headed youth of a rough subculture, is popularly seen as the sort to cause disorder.

clue.text: Plan constructed with care in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: something constructed is built afresh, so the letters of plan and care are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A carefully built plan is described in a particular way of talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular way of speaking or vocabulary, such as legal parlance.

clue.text: Places for diners are set, i.e. arranged

indicators.note: the letters of are set, i.e. are put into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: The tables in restaurants are laid ready, that is, neatly arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Eateries are restaurants and cafes, places where people go to dine.

clue.text: Current measure coming from a politician before

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: A political statement about current affairs comes from an MP earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere is the SI unit of electric current.

clue.text: Shakespearean prince in tiny community

definitions.meaning: the Prince of Denmark in Shakespeare's tragedy
a small village, smaller than a town

explanation.surface: A prince from a play turns up in a little village.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is both Shakespeare's Danish prince and the ordinary word for a small settlement.

clue.text: After end of food one performed

indicators.note: the word one comes after the letter from food
takes only the final letter of the word food

explanation.surface: Once the food was finished, someone gave a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Done means carried out or performed, as in a task done well.

clue.text: Place: it is located in the Home Counties

indicators.note: says the word it sits inside the letters for the region

parts.note: the Home Counties are the counties around London in south-east England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A location is found somewhere in the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties surrounding London, in the South East.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a place or location, such as a building site.
